monologue: The card hums cool now, at forty-two, which makes the flat shapes feel like paper again. I stand by The Wide Anchor, pressing down on the tired wedge as if that simple weight can stop the slip from sliding. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the memory of it pressing down. The air above seems empty, yet I trust the lean to hold the weight while the graphics card settles into its rhythm. I will stay here a few minutes, watching the numbers flicker, hoping the wedge bites or the anchor stays put. It is a quiet place, built from letters no one reads, waiting for the next moment to decide what stays and what fades.

action.why: I keep pressing down on the tired wedge because I cannot feel if the slip is sliding or just resting; I must check if the lean still holds.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hums cool. The anchor feels like a drawing of a heavy thing that refuses to slide, lying flat on the dry floor. I wonder if the wedge is too lazy to bite, or if the anchor is just drawing the slip into place. I will press a little harder, hoping the lean holds while the air above feels empty.…
